lastReleaseMessage: The Beacon's hum reaches the horde, a pooled Drowned splits off its route, the campaign save is read back, and thirty review findings close

items: Declared milestone moved M1 to M6 on 2026-08-26. M6 Art Integration is the track receiving the work and has been for weeks; M1 Vertical Slice stays open behind it. The old declaration paired M1 with a rule that the number only advances on a gameplay deliverable, which froze the number against a track nobody was on. The number now counts Roadmap deliverables across all nine milestones, so art work moves it.

How the 55 is derived, countable off the GDD Roadmap tab: 27 of 49 deliverables shipped. M0 8/8, M1 5/6, M2 2/4, M3 3/4, M4 6/8, M5 0/4, M6 3/5, M7 0/5, M8 0/5. Recounted 2026-09-23 after v0.73.0 struck three M3 deliverables (the mission rail, the inter-mission save now read back on the Campaign button, and the ten authored missions). The same counting rule applies, one struck Roadmap deliverable is one shipped item.

M1 Vertical Slice, five of six shipped. Kane ruled on 2026-09-22 (D82, D-OPEN-40) that the shipped missions are the milestone's target: 'basically done, we have missions added, I just need to test them.' The Roadmap deliverable that read 'Hold the Wall mission script (5-7 wave cadence)' now describes what shipped, the ten authored campaign missions under source/data/missions/campaign/ each with its own horde schedule (mission.gd horde_days since v0.65.0), and is struck. The Shambler and Lunger combat tuning pass shipped in v0.70.0 (Lunger 45 to 40 hit points, roster weights 3 and 2, reasoning on the Balance tab) and is struck; playtesting is Kane's. Open: Hatchery destruction + Coral Receding VFX, now a P1 backlog row for next week by his word (hatchery.gd is a scaffold with group membership, HP 800, a 2x2 footprint and four spawn constants; no spawn loop and no destruction handler exist).

M3 Intro Campaign, three of four shipped as of v0.73.0: the mission selection rail (v0.65.0), the inter-mission save, written after every mission since v0.65.0 and read back on the Campaign button since v0.73.0 (reliability-06), and the ten hand-authored missions. Open: the Leviathan Cyst and its boss fight, which waits on the enemy-structure work Kane put on next week (D82).

M6 Art Integration, three of five shipped. Building sprites, terrain tile set and HUD icon set are in. Open: unit sheets, where three of six scenes carry Spine rigs (scout, rifleman, marksman) and harpoonist, tommy and trench_sweeper carry none; and enemy sheets, where only the Shambler is rigged and the other seven are static single frames.

M4 Keepers, six of eight shipped and the milestone still in progress. The registry autoload, the housing-capacity draft trigger, the 80-card pool, the draft modal, the gold reroll and the exclusive and standalone card families are struck. Open: the keeper card art, so the modal ships on placeholder presentation, and the category filter on the skirmish setup screen.

Live defect inside the active track: tools/bake_spine_sheets.gd configures two bakes, shambler and scout, while rifleman.tscn and marksman.tscn both carry rigs. Past the eight-unit LIVE_RIG_BUDGET in source/units/unit_lod.gd a demoted rig has no baked sheet to fall back to. Queued as bar-raise-2026-08-24-rising-asset-pipeline-01, which names the Rifleman only.

Rifleman rig refresh. Navy calls the shipped Rifleman rig out of date (docs/ASSETS.md); the refresh needs her re-export from Spine Editor 4.3 with the standard clip set (Idle, Walk, NormalFire, RepeatFire and their Back facings) plus the death clip the current rig never had, then the baker run and the baked sheet committed. Until it lands the current rig and its baked sheet stay (art-direction-consistency-03).

barRaise.topFinding: The campaign that four releases built does not survive a restart: campaign.gd saves after every mission but nothing in source/ ever calls its load_from, so relaunching the game throws away every held site, record page and Faculty point while a valid save sits on disk (reliability-06). The same week's release back half also stopped short: v0.65.3 shipped with every version marker agreeing, yet the release marker, the dev-log post, the backlog notify and the audit digest still sit at v0.65.2, and release.ps1 now carries a duplicate play-test step whose first copy names a path that cannot exist. The first real profile of the played build reads about half the frame-rate target at the target load, but its own baseline drifted 27.8 percent, past the 15 percent limit the project set for trusting a bench. Hook the campaign load first; it is one call and it is the defect a player meets.

the playtest caveat is in README.md under Status: no mission places a Hatchery, Brood Mound or Leviathan Cyst, so there is nothing to clear and pressure arrives only on the wave director's clock, which makes a run read as pure defence. The build half needs placement rules and a Coral Receding specification that do not exist, and is carried as rising-keeper-structures-reach-a-spawn-site-2026-09-02;

the per-Node fallback now has a test that keeps it honest: it pins that all eight flags exist and default on, that the wave director still reads every one, that each per-Node scene resolves and carries the fields the branch depends on, and that the dispatcher keeps a per-Node exit. Both pools also warn once when they grow past their pre-allocated records, because the renderers hold fixed buffers.

both pools warn once when they grow past their pre-allocated records, naming that the renderer buffer does not grow with them so the overflow is live and undrawn; commit b2f78e3. Nothing referenced either old root name, checked across every .gd, .tscn and script in the repository before the change, and the 1974-test suite passes after it.

The history is measured and recorded: 424.93 MiB packed across 5,225 objects, against the 15.6 MB working tree the decision had been resting on. What it is made of settles the question rather than reopening it. Summing every blob version by path, docs/GDD.html accounts for 249.6 MB and CHANGELOG.md for 52.2 MB, two text documents rewritten in full on each of 344 releases, while the largest art file in the whole history is 6.8 MB. Roughly three quarters of the weight is text that large-file storage does not address. The decline stands and its first reason is stronger: rewriting 425 MiB of history on a repository with a live remote is a worse trade than it looked. The record also names the clone-size problem as a different job with different tools.

post-audit-digests.ps1 names #rising-audit, which is the channel its webhook is bound to. It printed #rising-resources, and the handler's own table records that the Resources webhook was never created.

Settled on #rising-backlog, and the two backlog scripts plus the release header are corrected to it. The handler's table won because it is the side that was checked against Discord and records which webhook is not created; the scripts carried a name copied from a sibling project whose category is shaped differently. The handler now says which side won and why. Only the printed string was ever affected, since routing follows the webhook file.

diagnose-gdd-publish.ps1 reads the live GATED_DOCS entry instead of the static file the key-value migration retired, which is why it reported MISSING on every run. It prints the live byte count, the live hash and the local hash of docs/GDD.html, and says DRIFT with both sizes when they disagree. Hash as well as size, because a publish that truncated or re-encoded the document keeps its length more often than not.

The gauntlet runs once per release. release.ps1 sets BR_PRESHIP_DONE after its own passing run, and the pre-commit hook stands down when it sees it. The direct call stays and the hook is the one that yields, because the hook lives under .git/ and is untracked: it can be missing on a fresh clone, and a release must not depend on a file that may not be there. The variable is set only for that process and its children, so a bare commit from any other shell still meets the whole wall, and a release that dies before committing takes the variable with it. push-to-github.ps1 also rewrites a hook that predates the change, since an untracked old copy would otherwise keep running the gauntlet twice on every machine that already had one.

Measured, then throttled. tools/bench_scale.gd gained a roaming case that keeps the whole roster walking for the sample window, plus a no-fog twin of it so the stamp could be attributed rather than guessed at. Forty units walking cost 32.89 ms over baseline with the fog on and 8.64 ms with it off, putting the stamp at 24.25 ms, or 0.61 ms per moving unit per frame against a 16.67 ms frame. The re-stamp threshold went from one pixel, which meant every frame for anything walking, to a quarter tile read off constants.TILE_W, which is the distance at which the low-resolution explored texture actually changes. Re-measured after: the roaming case fell from 32.89 ms to 8.90 ms against its no-fog twin at 8.18 ms, so the stamp now costs 0.72 ms for forty moving units, and the stationary case improved from 14.20 ms to 9.37 ms as well.

BACKLOG.md files Skirmish as M5, matching the design document's own milestone, and the version-one audio row is the design document's list. The row it replaced named convoy bells and a sortie horn, three of four describing mechanics cut in v0.38.0. Both rows say what was corrected and why the design document is the side that won.

The changelog tab has the search box, a bump filter and the shown-count the backlog and asset tabs already had. The entries are text separated by line breaks rather than elements, so the filter wraps each one in a span the first time it runs and filters spans after that, which keeps a 344-entry list responsive. Verified in a browser: 344 shown at rest, 1 for a phrase search that returned the right entry, 70 for the minor filter, and 344 again on clear.
source/units/trench_sweeper.tscn's root is TrenchSweeper. Nothing referenced the old name.

skirmish.tres is called Skirmish in the play menu and every save slot, and its briefing describes the mode rather than the art preview it stopped being: one Lantern, one map, no campaign orders, and a seed that replays the same ground.

save_load.gd gained _tile_in_bounds, and both _recreate_building and _recreate_unit refuse a saved tile that falls outside the live grid, warning with the class and the tile. Refuse rather than clamp: clamping stacks every out-of-bounds entity on one edge tile, which reads as a wall the player never built and is harder to explain than one that is missing, and the caller already reports a refusal the way it reports a missing scene. A grid that cannot say how big it is gets the benefit of the doubt, since the guard exists to catch a mismatch rather than to refuse a load. Nine checks in run_tests.gd cover the corners, the negatives, the unsized grid and the null grid; shipped in v0.70.0 with 1983 tests passing.
